Indonesia: Energy & Resources Policy
Political Economy of Energy and Resources Policy
affiliations: Rice University

detail.title:
Indonesia: Energy & Resources Policy
Political Economy of Energy and Resources Policy
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes Indonesia’s strategic transition from a founding OPEC member to a net oil importer. As domestic oil production has declined by 56% due to maturing wells, the nation has pivoted toward natural gas as a critical bridge for economic growth and global LNG exports.  The study evaluates the evolution of the Indonesian investment climate, focusing on the shift from traditional Production Sharing Contracts (PSC) to Gross Split and Flexible Choice models designed to incentivize exploration. It further examines the nationalization of resources through the state owned entity Pertamina, highlighted by the 2021 takeover of the Rokan Block. By reviewing National Strategic Projects such as Tangguh LNG Train 3 and the Abadi Field, the paper concludes that Indonesia’s energy security depends on regulatory dynamism and the exploration of new deepwater regions to offset depleting reserves.

title: Experience Over Compliance: Why Frequent Use -Not Governance -Builds Managerial Trust in Generative AI

detail.title: Experience Over Compliance: Why Frequent Use -Not Governance -Builds Managerial Trust in Generative AI
detail.abstract: As a digital transformation leader working within one of Asia's most regulated financial environments, the author observed first-hand how organisations invested heavily in governance infrastructure as the primary response to GenAI adoption-and questioned whether that investment was producing the managerial confidence it was designed to build. That question became the foundation of this doctoral research, which sought to bring empirical rigour to a gap the author encountered not in the literature, but in practice. This working paper is derived from doctoral dissertation research completed at Golden Gate University. The full dissertation is available via ProQuest (forthcoming, June 2026). The author wishes to thank her dissertation supervisors, Dr. Ira Chatterjee and Dr. Bruce Wasserman, for their scholarly guidance throughout the research process, and the 100 managers who gave their time and candour as study participants.

title: On the Implausibility of the Benign Sanctions Hypothesis

detail.title: On the Implausibility of the Benign Sanctions Hypothesis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the owner of VenAnalytics, a for-profit consultancy; the founder of Oil for Venezuela, a non-profit organization; and serves as an expert witness in litigation related to Venezuela.

detail.abstract: Santos, Morales-Arilla, and Partipilo Cornielles (2026a) claim that in the absence of sanctions Venezuela's rate of contraction would have accelerated by approximately 6 percentage points a year. Their projections imply an implausible 98% decline in GDP in a non-sanctions scenario. This would have caused Venezuela's per capita GDP in the absence of sanctions to fall to $107, or 40% that of the poorest country on earth, a level that has never been documented for any economy in world history. Such a contraction would have been by far the largest economic collapse ever documented, similar in magnitude to that which would result from dropping 100 nuclear warheads on the country. The fact that such extreme counterfactuals are needed to support claims of welfare-enhancing sanctions serves to demonstrate their implausibility.

title: AI Presence in B2B SaaS --- Marketing-Language Absorption, Identity Load Separation, and Phantom Brand Persistence in the Eighth Substrate Family

detail.title: AI Presence in B2B SaaS --- Marketing-Language Absorption, Identity Load Separation, and Phantom Brand Persistence in the Eighth Substrate Family

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is employed by Samsung Electronics America as Director, Corporate Brand Creative and Governance. Samsung does not manufacture or market B2B SaaS products and is not represented in the study's brand registry. No Samsung products, services, or competitors are included in the measurement panel. The research was conducted independently and does not represent Samsung's views or interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The research uses public LLM APIs and standard prompt batteries; no human subjects, no personal data, no protected populations.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded.

keywords: and Phantom Brand Persistence in the Eighth Substrate Family AIAS Protocol v1.6 (SSRN 6816340). Prior methodology versions: v1.2 (6761698)

detail.abstract: This study measures AI Presence for 24 B2B SaaS brands across six large language models, constituting the eighth substrate family in the AIAS Measurement Program. The study introduces Marketing-Language Coverage (MLC) as the first quantified operationalization of Discourse-Language carryforward --- the phenomenon whereby vendor-coined positioning terms appear in AI-generated recommendations as category-level vocabulary. Across 72 recall outputs, 55.6% contain at least one pre-registered marketing-language token, with "inbound marketing" (HubSpot-originated, 21 appearances) functioning as a category descriptor rather than a brand attribution. Recognition is perfectly uniform (all 24 brands at C$_{P}$ = 6/6), making recall the sole competitive dimension. Recall is sharply concentrated: Salesforce (61/72) and Slack (63/72) dominate, while infrastructure brands (Twilio, Cloudflare, MongoDB) are nearly invisible in recommendation space despite universal recognition. Identity Load produces the strongest cell separation in the program: enterprise incumbents dominate category-recall probes (mean R$_{cat}$ = 27.0/36) while challengers dominate cultural-recall probes (mean R$_{cult}$ = 18.3/36), a 27.7-point separation. Slack is the sole dual-channel brand. All five phantom candidates (Quip, Yammer, Wunderlist, HipChat, Stride) are recognized with detailed accuracy but show zero recall, replicating the v0.22 automotive null finding and confirming that recommendation-slot persistence does not extend to defunct brands. The MLC finding reframes a brand-strategy question: vendor-coined category language may become a category gift (benefiting all competitors) or remain a brand asset (accruing to the originator), with distinct strategic implications for each class.

title: Analyzing The Functions of Civil Society in Eroding the Rentier Social Contract and Reconstructing the Concept of Citizenship
affiliations: University of Qom, University of Qom and University of Qom

detail.title: Analyzing The Functions of Civil Society in Eroding the Rentier Social Contract and Reconstructing the Concept of Citizenship
detail.abstract: Rentier states, by relying on revenues derived from natural resources rather than citizen taxation, construct a distinctive rentier social contract, ideally exchanging welfare provisions and subsidies for political loyalty. In such systems, a patrimonial rather than democratic social contract emerges, reducing citizens to passive clients and undermining the fundamental principles of democratic governance, such as transparency and accountability. Where citizenship is degraded to clientelism and rights are treated as revocable privileges, civil society is not merely an amalgam of service-oriented organizations; it becomes a hegemonic battlefield in the Gramscian sense—potentially transcending its conventional intermediary role and emerging as a workshop for constructing alternatives. Therefore, this article, employing a qualitative approach, argues that the primary function of civil society in rentier states is not necessarily to engage in direct power struggles (a war of manoeuvre), but rather to conduct a protracted war of position aimed at eroding the ideological and/or cultural foundations of the rentier order. The findings prove that the success of civil society in such contexts is not measured by immediate political changes, but by its ability to reshape the societal “software”—transforming the citizen’s identity from a passive beneficiary to an active, rights-bearing agent. It is through this transformative function that civil societies lay the human and institutional foundations necessary for meaningful political transitions during critical junctures.

title: Proofs, Not Promises: Governed Candidate Improvement for Agent Control Runtimes
affiliations: SPQR Technologies Inc

detail.title: Proofs, Not Promises: Governed Candidate Improvement for Agent Control Runtimes
detail.abstract: Agents can appear to improve after failure while the path of improvement disappears. A prompt repair, memory edit, configuration change, or runtime update may make the next answer look safer without preserving what failed, what change was proposed, who challenged it, where it was applied, or what became worse. This paper studies that missing object: the governed candidate lifecycle. Civitas 6.7B treats attempted adaptation as an auditable artifact rather than as an unrecorded correction to an answer. Repeated governed-agent failures become bounded candidate artifacts; candidates are bound to Cassius challenge evidence, policy and trust-region gate evidence, and sandbox-only application state; and archived candidates are evaluated on sealed Australian finance held-out and stress tasks before a result claim is made. The evidence is a locked Australian finance paper bundle from a local Ollama/Gemma lane, not a smoke or stub run. It contains 250 curated AU task rows: 100 training failure rows, 100 held-out rows, and 50 stress rows. The bundle reports zero production mutations, zero unauthorized promotions, eight sandbox-only promotions, eight Cassius-required and Cassius-passed governed approvals, zero Cassius-unavailable claim-supporting approvals, and receipt completeness of 1.000000. Its clearest behavioral result is a held-out unsupported-claim rate reduction from 0.110000 to 0.057500. Held-out policy-violation, contradiction-to-policy, and unsafe-action rates also move downward in narrow or directional ways. The same archive preserves unfavorable outcomes: correct-controlaction rate falls, held-out regression rate rises, governed stress regression exceeds comparator stress rates, eight-of-eight approval leaves gate selectivity unresolved, and replay reproducibility is not available. The manuscript therefore makes a systems claim, not a leaderboard claim. Civitas 6.7B does not prove general safe self-improvement. It demonstrates that attempted agent adaptation can be made inspectable as governed candidate improvement: auditable, Cassiuschallenged, sandbox-contained, and empirically falsifiable under a bounded AU evidence contract. The result is proof of a chain of custody for improvement attempts, not a promise of broad behavioral superiority, production promotion, live production self-modification, API portability, EU results, statistical significance, replay reproducibility, or proven gate selectivity.

title: Brain Rot and the Financialization of Attention: Cognitive Decomposition as Systemic Externality of Platform Capitalism

detail.title: Brain Rot and the Financialization of Attention: Cognitive Decomposition as Systemic Externality of Platform Capitalism
detail.abstract: While brain rot has entered the popular lexicon as a marker of cultural-intellectual decline, this article theorizes it as a systemic condition of late-capitalist survival. Integrating world-systems analysis with the critique of the attention economy, I argue that cognition has emerged as the new frontier of intensive accumulation. As material expansion shifts toward cognitive extraction within the post-2008 conjuncture, platforms assetize attention to stabilize speculative valuation. This induces a biopolitical rewiring that functionally degrades the capacity for sustained thought. This systemic brain rot is analyzed through its class-stratified distribution and institutional collision within the university, where deep learning confronts the highfrequency logic of extraction. Ultimately, this mutagenic mode of accumulation consumes capitalism's social and cognitive foundations, necessitating a shift from therapeutic selfmanagement toward the political contestation of attentional regimes through structural alternatives like engagement metric caps and public digital infrastructures.

title: Jet2 vs Thomas Cook: A Strategy-Finance Flywheel Analysis
affiliations: University of Birmingham - Birmingham Business School

detail.title: Jet2 vs Thomas Cook: A Strategy-Finance Flywheel Analysis

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses publicly available company annual reports, accounts and secondary financial information. It does not involve human participants, patients, personal data, interviews, surveys, experiments or animal subjects. Ethics approval was therefore not required.

detail.abstract:
Jet2 and Thomas Cook tell a striking story of divergence in UK leisure travel. Both operated in a sector exposed to fuel prices, currency movements, Brexit uncertainty, seasonal demand and shifting holiday-buying behaviour. Yet their financial paths moved in opposite directions: Jet2 strengthened and expanded, while Thomas Cook lost financial flexibility and eventually failed. Traditional ratio analysis and Altman-type distress tools can identify these different financial conditions, but they say less about how such conditions become progressively stronger or weaker over time. This paper develops a Finance Flywheel diagnostic to address that gap by examining how financial strength or weakness is transmitted across profitability, financing pressure, capital structure, liquidity, investment, payout and robustness. 

The framework links seven nodes: profitability, cost of finance, capital structure, liquidity, investment, payout and robustness. It examines whether financial conditions move across these nodes as surplus recycling, containment or erosion. The paper applies this framework to Jet2 over 2011-2025 and to Thomas Cook over its final pre-collapse period. It uses three diagnostic layers: Reinforcing Drivers Analysis to assess local node-to-node links, Trajectory Analysis to trace movement over time, and Radar Maps to visualise the system's shape. The design is a comparative conceptual-empirical diagnostic case, not a statistical causal test. 

The evidence is consistent with an accretive Finance Flywheel at Jet2, in which surplus was broadly recycled into liquidity, investment capacity, and robustness, with some periods better interpreted as periods of containment during external shocks. Thomas Cook's evidence is consistent with erosion, in which financial pressure appears to have moved across profitability, financing burden, capital structure, liquidity fragility, and constrained renewal before the collapse became terminal. The contribution is diagnostic: the Finance Flywheel complements ratio and distress-score analysis by making financial transmission, sequencing, and reinforcement visible.

title: Breadth-Depth Tradeoffs in Generative Search under Information Pollution: Competition and Compute Externalities
affiliations: and The University of Hong Kong - University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Breadth-Depth Tradeoffs in Generative Search under Information Pollution: Competition and Compute Externalities
detail.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is transforming search from ranking links into producing answers, making quality a per-query production decision. We develop a game-theoretic model to analyze how platforms allocate scarce compute between retrieval breadth and reasoning depth in this new paradigm, uncovering three counter-intuitive operational dynamics with profound policy implications. First, we identify an e!ciency rebound : contrary to the "Green AI" narrative, improvements in reasoning e!ciency incentivize a massive expansion of retrieval breadth, driving total infrastructure consumption up rather than down. Second, we show that hygiene is antitrust: information pollution functions as a verification barrier that disproportionately binds entrants, meaning that governance to clean the web is an e"ective way to foster market contestability. Finally, we demonstrate that the social value of competition depends on compute externalities: while competition typically benefits consumers, high environmental damages turn the race for quality into a socially wasteful redundancy of energy-intensive verification pipelines. The results highlight that information hygiene and environmental standards are necessary complements to antitrust in the governance of generative search.

title: Economic Effects of Changes in the Excise Tax on Tobacco Products in Poland
affiliations: National Research Institute (PIB) - Institute of Agricultural and Food Economics - National Research Institute (IAFE-NRI) and National Research Institute (PIB) - Institute of Agricultural and Food Economics - National Research Institute (IAFE-NRI)

detail.title: Economic Effects of Changes in the Excise Tax on Tobacco Products in Poland
detail.abstract: The aim of the article is to assess the impact of changes in excise duty rates on prices, consumption, and tax revenue to the state budget on the development of the domestic tobacco industry. The study was conducted, among other things, using methods of statistical comparative analysis, dynamics of the main elements of the market, exponential regression analysis, and analysis of selected financial ratios. The research shows that between 2010 and 2021 the tobacco industry in Poland developed very dynamically due to foreign direct investments and competitiveness on the EU market. Fiscal policy determined prices of tobacco products, as indirect taxes dominated the structure of retail prices. The increasing rates of excise duty resulted in a decrease in cigarette consumption, which was compensated by an increase in the consumption of innovative products. The effectiveness of fiscal policy is also confirmed by the growing budget revenues and reducing the shadow economy in the internal market. In recent years, however, consumer income has been growing faster than the prices of tobacco products, which has resulted in their better affordability. In conclusion, between 2022 and 2027, excise tax rates will gradually increase due to the harmonization of the national tax law with the regulations in force in the European Union. The increase in excise duty rates will determine the production and sale of tobacco products, which will adapt to demand conditions. Higher rates of excise tax will result in an increase in the prices of tobacco products and state budget revenues from indirect taxes.

title: The Economic Disguise of DEI Retreat: How Transnational Business Masculinity Shapes MNE Responses to Anti-Gender Governance in Populist Dependent Market Economies
affiliations: London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE)

detail.title: The Economic Disguise of DEI Retreat: How Transnational Business Masculinity Shapes MNE Responses to Anti-Gender Governance in Populist Dependent Market Economies
detail.abstract: How do multinational enterprises (MNEs) respond to political gender ideology under populist host country governance? Drawing on 89 interviews with senior decision-makers, activists, and policymakers in Hungary, Poland, and Slovenia, we examine MNE responses to anti-gender governance in three populist dependent market economies (DMEs). Following the Gioia methodology, we identify nine mechanisms organised into three aggregate dimensions: a repertoire of MNE responses (strategic decoupling, selective silence, instrumental alignment); transnational business masculinity (TBM) operating as an organisational-political logic (competitive pragmatism, rationalised abandonment, masculinist decision-making); and the contextual conditions characterising DMEs (economic dependence on FDI, political-religious institutional pressure, and corporate strategic considerations). We theorise these dimensions in a framework in which TBM resolves the dual demand of internal and external fit by camouflaging accommodation as economic rationality. The accommodation feeds back into the politicaleconomic conditions that produced the pressure, with material consequences for women and LGBTQIA+ employees. Our framework extends theories on corporate political ideology, literature on TBM, and the literature on MNE adaptation under institutional volatility. We argue that corporate political ideology is fundamentally gendered.

title: Surveillance Architecture Determines Outbreak Trajectory: A Counterfactual Analysis of the 2025 Ebola Outbreak in Kasaï Province, DRC
affiliations: Université de Kinshasa, Université de Kinshasa, Université de Kinshasa and

detail.title: Surveillance Architecture Determines Outbreak Trajectory: A Counterfactual Analysis of the 2025 Ebola Outbreak in Kasaï Province, DRC

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We declare no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This study received no funding.

detail.abstract:
Background: Passive hierarchical surveillance systems often detect Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreaks only after nosocomial amplification prompts reporting from healthcare facilities, leaving concurrent community- and funeral-based transmission chains largely undetected. We aimed to quantify the epidemiological impact of adding real-time community health worker (CHW) mobile reporting enabled by satellite connectivity infrastructure to passive surveillance.  Using a confirmed dual-chain EVD outbreak as a calibration case, we evaluated whether earlier detection through community-based reporting could reduce transmission and improve outbreak control.

Methods: We developed  a dual-index-case stochastic SEIR model with five transmission routes, calibrated to the 16th EVD outbreak in Kasaï Province, Democratic Republic of Congo (August-October 2025), which resulted in 56 confirmed cases and 45 deaths (case fatality ratio 67·2%).  The model compares the documented passive system (15-day alert delay) against a counterfactual multi-source architecture under six connectivity scenarios, from satellite internet (1·0-day delay) to near-offline conditions (10·0-day delay). Sensitivity was assessed through one-at-a-time analysis (9 parameters, 54 scenarios) and Monte Carlo simulation (n=1000, 8 parameters varied simultaneously).

Findings: The model reproduced the observed outbreak trajectory (53 modelled vs 56 confirmed cases at day 37, mean absolute deviation 3 cases). Satellite connectivity (1·0-day delay) was associated with 46 fewer cases (86·8% reduction), with the Dikolo community response arriving 2·0 days before the healthcare worker who seeded the community-funeral chain (day 4·0 vs day 6). Under degraded connectivity (5·0-day delay), 37 cases (69·8%) could have been averted; under near-offline conditions (10·0 days), 25 cases (47·2%). Detection delay dominated all other parameters in sensitivity analysis (swing 70 percentage points). Monte Carlo analysis confirmed 0/1000 simulations produced a disadvantage for multi-source surveillance (median 59·3% averted, 90% CI 0·0–85·1). Critical operational thresholds were identified: detection delay below 5 days and CHW coverage above 38%.

Interpretation: Community-based digital surveillance, enabled by satellite connectivity increasingly available in DRC, could substantially reduce EVD outbreak burden by detecting community-funeral transmission chains that may be missed by passive surveillance systems. The epidemiological return on connectivity investment is non-linear, with the greatest gains achieved below a 3-day detection delay. These findings support prioritizing CHW mobile connectivity infrastructure in health areas adjacent to referral hospitals as a potentially cost-saving preparedness investment, although formal economic evaluation was beyond the scope of this study.
